passages.text: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with difficult questions.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon.
She heard about his fame.
She heard that his fame was connected to the name of the LORD.
The queen of Sheba decided to come to Solomon.
She wanted to test Solomon.
She tested him with difficult questions.
passages.original: וּמַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֗א שֹׁמַ֛עַת אֶת־ שֵׁ֥מַע שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וַתָּבֹ֥א לְנַסֹּת֖וֹ בְּחִידֽוֹת׃

passages.text: She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones. So she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was on her mind.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba traveled to Jerusalem.
She brought a very large caravan with her.
Many camels came with her.
The camels carried spices.
The camels also carried much gold.
The camels carried precious stones.
The queen of Sheba came to Solomon.
She spoke to Solomon.
She told him everything that was on her mind.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֣א יְרוּשָׁלְַ֗מָה בְּחַיִל֮ כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹד֒ גְּ֠מַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב רַב־ מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבֹא֙ אֶל־ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־ לְבָבָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was wise.
The queen of Sheba asked Solomon many questions.
Solomon answered every question.
Nothing was hidden from Solomon.
Solomon explained everything to her.
No question was too hard for Solomon to answer.
passages.original: וַיַּגֶּד־ לָ֥הּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת־ כָּל־ דְּבָרֶ֑יהָ לֹֽא־ הָיָ֤ה דָּבָר֙ נֶעְלָ֣ם מִן־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א הִגִּ֖יד לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built, the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants and cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba visited Solomon in Jerusalem.
She saw all the wisdom of Solomon.
She saw the palace that Solomon had built.
She saw the food on Solomon’s table.
She saw where his servants sat.
She saw how his attendants stood to serve him.
She saw the clothing of his attendants.
She saw his cupbearers.
She saw the burnt offerings Solomon brought up at the house of the LORD.
All these things amazed her.
She was left without breath.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת כָּל־ חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָֽה׃ וּמַאֲכַ֣ל שֻׁלְחָנ֡וֹ וּמוֹשַׁ֣ב עֲבָדָיו֩ וּמַעֲמַ֨ד מְשָׁרְתוֹ וּמַלְבֻּֽשֵׁיהֶם֙ וּמַשְׁקָ֔יו וְעֹ֣לָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא־ הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ ע֖וֹד רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba spoke to King Solomon.
She said, "The report I heard in my own country is true.
I heard about your words.
I heard about your wisdom.
What I heard was true."
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֱמֶת֙ הָיָ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בְּאַרְצִ֑י עַל־ דְּבָרֶ֖יךָ וְעַל־ חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me. Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba spoke to King Solomon.
She said she did not believe the reports about him at first.
She did not trust what she heard until she came to Jerusalem.
She saw everything with her own eyes.
She realized the reports did not tell her even half the truth.
Solomon’s wisdom was greater than she had heard.
His prosperity was also greater than the reports.
What she saw in person was far more than what she had been told.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ הֶאֱמַ֣נְתִּי לַדְּבָרִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֙אתִי֙ וַתִּרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינַ֔י וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹֽא־ הֻגַּד־ לִ֖י הַחֵ֑צִי הוֹסַ֤פְתָּ חָכְמָה֙ וָט֔וֹב אֶל־ הַשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

passages.text: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was wise.
\r\nHe ruled Israel.
\r\nThe queen of Sheba spoke to him.
\r\nShe said his men are blessed.
\r\nShe said his servants are blessed.
\r\nThese servants stand before Solomon all the time.
\r\nThey hear Solomon’s wisdom.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֲנָשֶׁ֔יךָ אַשְׁרֵ֖י עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה הָֽעֹמְדִ֤ים לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ תָּמִ֔יד הַשֹּׁמְעִ֖ים אֶת־ חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD’s eternal love for Israel, He has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD deserves blessing.
The LORD has found joy in you.
The LORD chose you.
The LORD set you on the throne of Israel.
The LORD loves Israel forever.
Because of His love, the LORD made you king.
The LORD made you king to do justice.
The LORD made you king to do righteousness.
passages.original: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ בָּר֔וּךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ חָפֵ֣ץ בְּךָ֔ לְתִתְּךָ֖ עַל־ כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּאַהֲבַ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְעֹלָ֔ם וַיְשִֽׂימְךָ֣ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

passages.text: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again was such an abundance of spices brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba visited King Solomon.
She gave King Solomon 120 talents of gold.
She gave him a very large amount of spices.
She also gave him precious stones.
No one ever brought so many spices again.
No one brought as many spices as the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
passages.original: וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים׀ כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֗ב וּבְשָׂמִ֛ים הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה לֹא־ בָא֩ כַבֹּ֨שֶׂם הַה֥וּא עוֹד֙ לָרֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־ נָתְנָ֥ה מַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֖א לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: (The fleet of Hiram that brought gold from Ophir also brought from Ophir a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.
passages.sermon:
King Hiram ruled in Tyre.
Hiram sent a fleet of ships to Ophir.
These ships brought gold from Ophir.
The fleet also brought a large amount of almug wood from Ophir.
The fleet brought precious stones from Ophir.
passages.original: וְגַם֙ אֳנִ֣י חִירָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ נָשָׂ֥א זָהָ֖ב מֵאוֹפִ֑יר הֵבִ֨יא מֵאֹפִ֜יר עֲצֵ֧י אַלְמֻגִּ֛ים הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָֽה׃

passages.text: The king made the almug wood into steps for the house of the LORD and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had such almug wood been brought in, nor has such been seen to this day.)
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
King Solomon received almug wood from Ophir.
King Solomon used the almug wood to make steps for the house of the LORD.
He also made steps for his own palace from the almug wood.
King Solomon made lyres from the almug wood.
He made harps for the singers from the almug wood.
No one had ever brought such almug wood before.
No one has seen such almug wood up to this day.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת־ עֲצֵ֨י הָאַלְמֻגִּ֜ים מִסְעָ֤ד לְבֵית־ יְהוָה֙ וּלְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכִנֹּר֥וֹת וּנְבָלִ֖ים לַשָּׁרִ֑ים לֹ֣א בָֽא־ כֵ֞ן עֲצֵ֤י אַלְמֻגִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א נִרְאָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired—whatever she asked—besides what he had given her out of his royal bounty. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
The queen of Sheba visited King Solomon.
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted.
He gave her whatever she asked for.
He also gave her gifts from his royal bounty.
After this, the queen of Sheba left Solomon.
She returned to her own country.
Her servants went with her.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן לְמַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֗א אֶת־ כָּל־ חֶפְצָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔לָה מִלְּבַד֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־ לָ֔הּ כְּיַ֖ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַתֵּ֛פֶן וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ׃ס

passages.text: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents, not including the revenue from the merchants, traders, and all the Arabian kings and governors of the land.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon received gold every year.
The gold weighed 666 talents.
This amount did not include other income.
Merchants brought more revenue.
Traders also brought more revenue.
All the kings of Arabia gave more revenue.
The governors of the land gave more revenue too.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵׁ֖שׁ כִּכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב׃ לְבַד֙ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֣י הַתָּרִ֔ים וּמִסְחַ֖ר הָרֹכְלִ֑ים וְכָל־ מַלְכֵ֥י הָעֶ֖רֶב וּפַח֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the king of Israel.
\r\nKing Solomon made two hundred large shields.
\r\nHe used hammered gold to make these shields.
\r\nEach shield contained six hundred shekels of gold.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה מָאתַ֥יִם צִנָּ֖ה זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֑וּט שֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־ הַצִּנָּ֥ה הָאֶחָֽת׃

passages.text: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made three hundred small shields.
He used hammered gold to make these shields.
Each shield contained three minas of gold.
King Solomon placed these shields in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
passages.original: וּשְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֤וֹת מָֽגִנִּים֙ זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֔וּט שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת מָנִים֙ זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־ הַמָּגֵ֣ן הָאֶחָ֑ת וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בֵּ֖ית יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃פ

passages.text: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the king of Israel.
King Solomon made a great throne.
He made the throne from ivory.
He covered the throne with pure gold.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ כִּסֵּא־ שֵׁ֖ן גָּד֑וֹל וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֥ב מוּפָֽז׃

passages.text: The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made a throne.
The throne had six steps.
The back of the throne was rounded at the top.
There was a seat on the throne.
There was an armrest on each side of the seat.
A lion stood beside each armrest.
passages.original: שֵׁ֧שׁ מַעֲל֣וֹת לַכִּסֵּ֗ה וְרֹאשׁ־ עָגֹ֤ל לַכִּסֵּה֙ מֵאַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְיָדֹ֛ת מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה אֶל־ מְק֣וֹם הַשָּׁ֑בֶת וּשְׁנַ֣יִם אֲרָי֔וֹת עֹמְדִ֖ים אֵ֥צֶל הַיָּדֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made a throne.
The throne had six steps.
Twelve lions stood on the steps.
There was one lion at each end of every step.
No other kingdom had ever made anything like this.
passages.original: וּשְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר אֲרָיִ֗ים עֹמְדִ֥ים שָׁ֛ם עַל־ שֵׁ֥שׁ הַֽמַּעֲל֖וֹת מִזֶּ֣ה וּמִזֶּ֑ה לֹֽא־ נַעֲשָׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן לְכָל־ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃

passages.text: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nAll of King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold.
\r\nAll of the utensils in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold.
\r\nThere was no silver used.
\r\nPeople did not value silver during Solomon’s days.
\r\nThey considered silver to be nothing.
passages.original: וְ֠כֹל כְּלֵ֞י מַשְׁקֵ֨ה הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ זָהָ֔ב וְכֹ֗ל כְּלֵ֛י בֵּֽית־ יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנ֖וֹן זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר אֵ֣ין כֶּ֗סֶף לֹ֥א נֶחְשָׁ֛ב בִּימֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לִמְאֽוּמָה׃

passages.text: For the king had the ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nHe was very wealthy and wise.
\r\nHe had ships called the ships of Tarshish.
\r\nThese ships belonged to King Solomon.
\r\nThe ships sailed on the sea.
\r\nThey sailed together with the fleet of Hiram.
\r\nHiram was the king of Tyre.
\r\nOnce every three years, the ships of Tarshish returned.
\r\nThe ships brought gold.
\r\nThe ships brought silver.
\r\nThe ships brought ivory.
\r\nThe ships brought apes.
\r\nThe ships brought peacocks.
passages.original: כִּי֩ אֳנִ֨י תַרְשִׁ֤ישׁ לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בַּיָּ֔ם עִ֖ם אֳנִ֣י חִירָ֑ם אַחַת֩ לְשָׁלֹ֨שׁ שָׁנִ֜ים תָּב֣וֹא׀ אֳנִ֣י תַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ נֹֽשְׂאֵת֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף שֶׁנְהַבִּ֥ים וְקֹפִ֖ים וְתֻכִּיִּֽים׃

passages.text: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was a king of Israel.
King Solomon became greater than all the other kings on earth.
He had more riches than any other king.
He had more wisdom than any other king.
passages.original: וַיִּגְדַּל֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ לְעֹ֖שֶׁר וּלְחָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nGod gave Solomon great wisdom.
\r\nGod placed this wisdom in Solomon’s heart.
\r\nPeople from every nation wanted to meet Solomon.
\r\nThey came to hear Solomon’s wisdom.
\r\nThey knew God had given Solomon this wisdom.
passages.original: וְכָ֨ל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה לִשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ אֶת־ חָכְמָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was greater than all other kings in riches and wisdom.
People from every nation came to see Solomon.
Each visitor brought a gift to Solomon every year.
They brought silver objects.
They brought gold objects.
They brought clothing.
They brought weapons.
They brought spices.
They brought horses.
They brought mules.
passages.original: וְהֵ֣מָּה מְבִאִ֣ים אִ֣ישׁ מִנְחָת֡וֹ כְּלֵ֣י כֶסֶף֩ וּכְלֵ֨י זָהָ֤ב וּשְׂלָמוֹת֙ וְנֵ֣שֶׁק וּבְשָׂמִ֔ים סוּסִ֖ים וּפְרָדִ֑ים דְּבַר־ שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king in Jerusalem.
Solomon gathered many chariots and horses.
He collected 1,400 chariots.
He collected 12,000 horses.
He placed some chariots and horses in special cities for chariots.
He kept some chariots and horses with him in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ וַיְהִי־ ל֗וֹ אֶ֤לֶף וְאַרְבַּע־ מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּשְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּנְחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled in Jerusalem.
He made silver very common in the city.
Silver became as plentiful as stones.
He also brought in many cedar trees.
Cedar became as abundant as sycamore trees in the foothills.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֶת־ הַכֶּ֛סֶף בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב׃

passages.text: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue; the royal merchants purchased them from Kue.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nSolomon owned many horses.
\r\nSolomon’s horses came from Egypt.
\r\nSolomon’s horses also came from Kue.
\r\nThe king’s merchants bought horses from Kue.
\r\nThe king’s merchants paid a price for the horses.
passages.original: וּמוֹצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕ה סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יִקְח֥וּ מִקְוֵ֖ה בִּמְחִֽיר׃

passages.text: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, they exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
passages.sermon:
A chariot from Egypt cost six hundred shekels of silver.
A horse from Egypt cost one hundred fifty shekels of silver.
The merchants exported chariots and horses from Egypt.
They sold them to all the kings of the Hittites.
They also sold them to the kings of Aram.
passages.original: וַֽ֠תַּעֲלֶה וַתֵּצֵ֨א מֶרְכָּבָ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת כֶּ֔סֶף וְס֖וּס בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמֵאָ֑ה וְ֠כֵן לְכָל־ מַלְכֵ֧י הַחִתִּ֛ים וּלְמַלְכֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם בְּיָדָ֥ם יֹצִֽאוּ׃פ
